paper_title: Improvement in the Efficiency of Alkylsilyl Functionalized Copolymer for Polymer Solar Cells: Face-On Orientation Enhanced by Random Copolymerization

knowledge_points.content: A D-A1-D-A2 type random copolymer was synthesized using silicon-containing benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b]dithiophene (Si-BDT) as the donor unit, and fluorobenzotriazole (TZ) and benzo[1,2-c:4,5-c]dithiophene-4,8-dione (BDD) as the two acceptor units.
knowledge_points.evidence: Two D-A1-D-A2-type random copolymers PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 were prepared by a Si-containing (Si-BDT) as a D unit, a TZ as an A1 unit, and copolymerized with 5% or 10% mole ratios of BDD as an A2 unit.

knowledge_points.content: The random copolymer PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19, when blended with the non-fullerene acceptor ITIC, achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 11.02%, with a VOC of 0.93 V, JSC of 17.56 mA cm⁻², and a fill factor (FF) of 67.48%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The best power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 11.02% was achieved for the PBDT-TZ-BDD1/19 : ITIC-based inverted device... (Jsc = 17.56 mAcm−2, Voc = 0.93 V, FF = 67.48% and PCE = 11.02%).

knowledge_points.content: Incorporating the planar BDD unit into the J71 polymer matrix effectively downshifts the HOMO levels from -5.40 eV (J71) to -5.42 eV (PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19) and -5.44 eV (PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9).
knowledge_points.evidence: The HOMOs were -5.40, -5.42, and -5.44 eV for J71, PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19, and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of BDD units increases the absorption coefficient of the polymer films from 0.96 × 10⁵ cm⁻¹ (J71) to 1.03 × 10⁵ cm⁻¹ (PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19) and 1.06 × 10⁵ cm⁻¹ (PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9).
knowledge_points.evidence: addition of BDD units did not reduce the absorption intensity of random copolymers but increased the film absorption coefficient in the following order: J71 (0.96 × 105 cm−1) < PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 (1.03 × 105 cm−1) < PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 (1.06 × 105 cm−1).

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis revealed that the addition of 5% BDD in PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 increased the pi-pi stacking coherence length (CCL) to 16.281 Å compared to 15.823 Å for the binary J71 polymer.
knowledge_points.evidence: The CCL (010) values for J71, PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19, and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 were estimated to be 15.823, 16.281, and 14.662 Å, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19:ITIC blend films exhibit higher and more balanced charge mobilities (hole mobility: 5.60 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹; electron mobility: 4.12 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) compared to the J71:ITIC system.
knowledge_points.evidence: The hole mobilities were 3.89 × 10−4, 5.60 × 10−4, and 3.78 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1... The electron mobilities were 2.02 × 10−4, 4.12 × 10−4, and 2.71 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1 for J71, PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Random copolymerization with BDD improves compatibility with the ITIC acceptor, resulting in a more homogeneous fibril-like nanophase separation and lower surface roughness (1.18 nm) compared to the J71:ITIC blend (2.03 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: the PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19: ITIC and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9: ITIC blend films were slightly smoother with a lower root-mean-square roughness (Rq) (1.18 nm for PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19: ITIC... than the J71:ITIC film (2.03 nm).

knowledge_points.content: A high content of BDD (10% in PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9) leads to a decrease in device performance compared to 5% BDD due to an excessively irregular sequence distribution that reduces polymer crystallinity.
knowledge_points.evidence: When the BDD content increased to 10%, the more irregular sequence caused less efficient pathway for charge transport... PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 neat film displayed the weakest (010) peak with the widest FWHM (010) and smallest CCL (010).

knowledge_points.content: The random copolymers PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 demonstrate high thermal stability with 5% weight loss decomposition temperatures (Td) exceeding 430 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: The copolymer PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/19 and PBDT-TZ-BDD-1/9 showed thermal decomposition temperatures (Td) at 5% weight loss above 430 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The silyl-functionalized donor unit (Si-BDT) utilizes sigma*-n* bond interactions to downshift energy levels and enhance the crystallinity of the resulting copolymers.
knowledge_points.evidence: The σ* (Si)-n* (C) bond interaction is demonstrated to not only effectively downshift the energy levels but also to improve the crystallinity of the copolymers and facilitate the charge transport.
